issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated instead of imported from its true source
issues.detail: The constant was previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat. The move re-declares it on Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and the writer now imports it from there. Two copies of the same magic number in sibling classes is the classic data-duplication smell. Either keep one canonical definition (in the flat format) and import it across the module boundary, or document why the value is independent.

issues.description: Public abstract class OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues now has package-private fields but remains public API
issues.detail: The class is still `public abstract` and has a public subclass DenseOffHeapVectorValues, yet the move dropped `protected` from the shared fields. External subclasses (or even subclasses in other packages within the module) can no longer access dimension, size, slice, etc. If the class is truly internal now, make it package-private; if it stays public, restore protected. The current shape is inconsistent.

issues.description: Two RW test scaffolds (V0 and V1) duplicate format wiring rather than parameterizing one
issues.detail: Lucene99RWV0HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat and Lucene99RWV1HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat are almost the same class with one decision (which writer to call) differing. This is the inheritance-as-switch antipattern. A single RW format taking a writer-version enum or factory would be smaller, more obvious, and easier to extend when the next legacy version lands.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throwing UnsupportedOperationException is correct shape but leaves dead constructor params
issues.detail: The format kept its full multi-arg constructors including numMergeWorkers/mergeExec, then removed the fields they used to populate, and the writer now throws. The constructors accept arguments that the format silently discards. Either drop the constructor parameters that no longer do anything, or document that they exist only for source compatibility with old callers. Right now the data structure (the constructor signature) lies about behavior.

issues.description: Lucene99RWV1 constructor hardcodes DEFAULT_MAX_CONN/DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH instead of using passed maxConn/beamWidth
issues.detail: The parameterized constructor accepts maxConn and beamWidth but fieldsWriter builds Lucene99HnswVectorsWriter with Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat.DEFAULT_MAX_CONN and DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH. If this is intentional for the legacy V1 reproduction, a comment is warranted; if not, it's a silent bug that will surface when a test passes non-default graph params.

review.summary: The move to backward_codecs is the right shape: read-only legacy format, writer in test scope, SPI registration updated. Data structure is mostly sound. Two concerns earn attention: a duplicated magic constant across sibling format classes (data should live in one place), and the OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues class being publicly extensible while its fields became package-private — inconsistent contract. The test-side RW scaffolding has grown two near-identical subclasses where one parameterized class would be smaller and clearer. Nothing here is too clever; the issues are about right-sizing the boundaries.
